newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM DEFENDS MPS' ENTITLEMENTS
The Prime Minister, John Howard, says some of the criticism of the entitlements enjoyed by MPs is unfounded and petty.
He has dismissed suggestions of wide-scale expense rorting by politicians.
Mr Howard has told Sydney Radio Station 2UE the rules allow MPs to use their entitlements for a whole range of purposes.
EMERGENCY WORKERS PREPARE FOR CYCLONE JUSTIN
Emergency workers along the north Queensland coast are sandbagging seaboard homes in preparation for Tropical Cyclone Justin.
At Innisfail's Flying Fish Point workers are trying to protect about 15 houses and strong winds and big seas are lifing water into some coastal streets in the Mackay district.
Guests have left the Hinchinbrook Island resort, off Cardwell, leaving seven staff behind to make sure everything is secure.
The head of the Counter Disaster Committee in the Townsville district says evacuation centres will open if the threat of storm surges increases.
The Weather Bureau says the Category 2 cyclone should intensify slightly before it heads towards the coast, but they're not expecting any big moves today.
It remains 580 kilometres east of Cairns.
BEAZLEY SAYS ARMY TRAINING FOR UNEMPLOYED A GIMMICK
The Federal Opposition has dismissed as a gimmick, the Prime Minister's proposal that basic military training could be an option in its work-for-the-dole scheme.
The Prime Minister says the government is keen to consider any proposal to reduce youth unemployment, including military training.
Opposition leader Kim Beazley says the military operates in a high-tech battlefield these days and can't be expected to expand its role as a basic trainer.
MINISTER DISMISSES JUNIOR DOCTOR CLAIMS
The Federal Health Minister, has rejected claims by junior doctors that the Government's move to make extra training for new General Practitioners mandatory, threatens their employment chances.
More than two-thousand young doctors in New South Wales are taking industrial action for a week, forcing elective surgery to be postponed in hospitals.
Minister, Dr Michael Wooldridge, says every junior doctor is guaranteed a training position.
Dr Wooldridge says it's not unreasonable, however, to think that they might just have to do a bit of community service to make a career out of it.
The Federal Opposition say the issue of restricting medicare provider numbers has been poorly handled by the Government.
TEN ESCAPE SYDNEY DETENTION CENTRE
Ten people have escaped from the Immigration Department's Villawood Detention Centre, in Sydney's west.
Police say the escapees, Nigerian nationals, left the centre around lunchtime.
It's believed four of them got onto a train leaving Villawood Station.
Police highway patrols and a helicopter are searching the area.
BOND PROSECUTION LAWYER SOUGHT BRIBE: COURT TOLD

The District Court in Perth has been told a former lawyer with the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions corruptly sought a two million dollar bribe from the son of Alan Bond, in return for confidential information about investigations into his father.

Michael Thomas Crowley has pleaded not guilty to two charges which allege he used his position as a legal officer on a Bond investigation taskforce in 1995 to photocopy and publish highly confidential material.

The Court heard Mr Crowley offered to give documents in return for two million dollars to Bond's son John, who subsequently found a bundle of papers left outside his Peppermint Grove home, relating to investigations into the billion dollar Bell Resources fraud.
Prosecutor John McKechnie QC, said that while in hindsight the plan might seem amateurish, if John Bond had not been honest, it may never have come to light.
OZ MEDAL HOPES GOOD FOR C'WEALTH GAMES
Sporting Officials say Australia's medal hopes for next year's Commonwealth Games have been boosted by the inclusion of six new sports.
Australia's campaign for the 1998 Games in Kuala Lumpur has been launched by the Prime Minister at a luncheon in Sydney.
Hockey, netball, squash, ten-pin bowling, rugby, and one day cricket will be added to the Games' program, while women's pole vault, hammer throw and triple jump will be included in athletic events.
Australian Commonwealth Games Association President Ray Godkin says Australia's excellence in the new sports augers well for its medal tally at the games.
